styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Grand Mosque, souks and the corniche.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Old Kuwait, museums and the towers.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Machboos, fish markets and sweet shops.

stays.why: Central and close to the souks and corniche; bus 13 from the airport stops here.
Lively shopping and café district; good for families and evening walks.
Business district with the towers and waterfront; handy for meetings.
Quiet residential spot between the centre and Salmiya; good value.

food: Try Kuwaiti machboos (spiced rice with meat or fish) and mutabbaq samak, a rice-and-fish dish.
Souq Sharq and the old Mubarakiya market are good for dates, spices and cheap local snacks.
Fish is a local staple; look for grilled hammour or zubaidi at seafood restaurants.
Cheap eats: shawarma and Indian or Pakistani cafeterias, often a few KWD a meal.
Alcohol is not sold in Kuwait. Expect juice bars and strong Arabic coffee instead.
more_time: Swap a city afternoon for the Kuwait Towers and the corniche walk at sunset.
Add a half-day to the Grand Mosque and the Tareq Rajab Museum of Islamic art.
Families can swap a souk visit for the Scientific Center aquarium and its dhow harbour.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the Grand Mosque, the souks and the corniche at a comfortable pace; add a night for museums and a beach day.

month_notes: January: cool and mild, highs near 19°C. Best month for walking the old town.
February: still mild, around 21°C, with a few rain days. Pack a light layer.
March: warming to 25°C. Pleasant for souks and the corniche.
April: hot at 31°C by day. Do outdoor sights in the morning.
May: 38°C and dry. Move between air-conditioned malls and museums.
June: very hot, 43°C. Keep outdoor time to early morning or after dark.
July: the hottest month, 45°C. Plan indoor days and short taxi rides.
August: still extreme at 44°C. Stay near the hotel pool or malls.
September: 41°C, slowly easing. Evenings are still hot.
October: down to 35°C. Better for the corniche after sunset.
November: comfortable at 26°C. Good month for markets and walks.
December: mild at 20°C with a few rain days. Bring a jacket for evenings.

climate_guide.summary: Hot desert climate: long, very hot summers, mild winters and almost no rain.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Highs of 19–26°C and cool evenings. Ideal for souks, the corniche and walking.

items.title: Summer is extreme (June to September)
items.text: Highs of 41–45°C. Plan indoor sights by day and go out only early or late.

items.title: Very little rain
items.text: A few rain days between November and March. No umbrella needed most of the year.

items.title: Dusty winds possible
items.text: Dust can haze the sky in spring and summer. Check conditions before desert trips.

items.title: Strong sun
items.text: Sun is intense even in winter. Use sunscreen, a hat and water.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, a light layer for winter nights and cool indoor AC, and modest dress for mosques.

transit.best: Taxis or ride apps for most trips; buses if you are saving money.

modes.text: No metro or tram. Don't plan around rail.
KPTC and CityBus share routes: about 300 fils in town, 350 fils longer. Bus 13 links the airport to Mirqab in about 1 hour.
Taxis ignore meters, so agree the fare first; orange taxis start near KD 1. Careem and Uber operate; check coverage locally.
Driving is common but traffic is heavy. Check licence rules before booking.
Fine only in cooler months, and the city is spread out. Use taxis in summer.
